title: Impact of Institutional Ownership on Firm Value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use an instrumental variable (IV) approach to identify the causal impact of institutional ownership on firm value. The inclusion status in the S&P 500 index (z) will be used as an instrument for institutional ownership (x). The key assumption for this approach is that the instrument (z) is correlated with the endogenous variable (x) and is exogenous, meaning it affects the dependent variable (y) only through its effect on the endogenous variable (x). In this case, we assume that being included in the S&P 500 index increases institutional ownership, but does not directly affect firm value.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(AER)
library(lmtest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s80_data.csv")

# First stage regression: institutional ownership (x) on S&P 500 inclusion status (z) and controls
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)

# Second stage regression: firm value (y) on predicted institutional ownership (x) from first stage and controls
second_stage <- lm(y ~ predict(first_stage, newdata = data) + controls, data = data)

# Print the coefficient of the predicted institutional ownership in the second stage regression
summary(second_stage)$coefficients[2, 1]

# Robustness check: test for overidentifying restrictions (Sargan test)
overid_test <- bptest(second_stage, ~ z | controls, data = data)
overid_test$statistic
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the coefficient of the predicted institutional ownership in the second stage regression to be negative, indicating that increased institutional ownership negatively affects firm value. The magnitude of the effect will depend on the strength of the relationship between institutional ownership and firm value, as well as the strength of the instrument. If the instrument is strong and the relationship between institutional ownership and firm value is significant, we expect a substantial negative effect. However, the exact magnitude is difficult to predict without more information about the underlying relationships in the data.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use S&P 500 inclusion as an instrument for institutional ownership.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased institutional ownership, driven by index inclusion, leads to a decrease in firm value.
